title: Mirror and Slide
description: Pairs practise staying in a low defensive stance while the defender mirrors an offensive partner's movements inside a small box.

content.objective: Stay in a low, balanced defensive stance and slide the feet without crossing them to stay in front of an attacker.
content.setup: Each pair works inside a box marked by four cones, about three metres square. One player is the offensive player without a ball, the other is the defender directly in front of them.
instructions: The offensive player moves left, right, forward or back inside the box at a controlled pace.
The defender mirrors each movement using slide steps without crossing the feet, staying an arm's length away.
After twenty seconds, switch roles for a second set of twenty seconds.
Increase the speed of the offensive player for the second round and add sudden changes of direction.
Finish with a one-minute race in which each defender tries to stay ahead of the attacker.
coachingPoints: Low stance: knees bent, hips low, back straight, chest up.
Slide without crossing the feet; push off the trailing leg.
Eyes on the chest of the attacker, not on the feet.
Hands active, one in the passing lane and one near the ball.
commonMistakes: Crossing the feet and losing balance.
Watching the attacker's feet and being beaten by a fake.
content.safety: Pairs stay in their own box and keep others clear; the attacker never moves faster than the defender can handle at the start.
progressions: Give the attacker a ball and allow a dribble inside the box.
regressions: Attacker moves slowly on a line with no direction changes.
variations: Play a mirror game in which the attacker tries to break away and the defender tries to hold them.

annotations.text: Slide, do not cross the feet
